e=e2-e1e = B0av

Let 2a be the side of the triangle and b the length AE.



AH AE = GH EC

∴ GH = AH AE EC

or GH = b - vt b · a

= a - a b vt

questions.solution:
Initially, the current was zero, so self-induced flux was also zero. Now when we rotate the loop, the change in flux is

Δϕ=2πR2×B

Finally, to maintain the same zero flux, the current in the superconducting loop will be such that the flux due to induced current will negative of the flux due to external field

L×i=2πR2×B.

i=2πR2×BL

questions.q: As shown in figure, the two parallel conducting rails, in a horizontal plane, are connected at one end by an inductor of inductance L. A slider (metallic) of mass m, is imparted a velocity v0, upon the rails, as shown in figure. The period of oscillation of the conducting rod is
questions.solution:
From energy conservation (there are no dissipative forces)-

E=12mv2+12LI2

⇒m2×2vdvdt+L2×2IdIdt=0

mvdvdt=-ILdIdt

The emf induced in an inductor is

E=LdIdt=Blv

⇒LdIdt=Bldxdt⇒LdI=Bldx⇒I=BlLx

The force acting on a current-carrying conductor is

mdvdt=-IBl

⇒dvdt=-IBlm

Substituting the value of I we get

dvdt=-BlLxBlm⇒a=-B2l2mLx

We got acceleration in the form of

a=-ω2x 

this implies that the motion is SHM, with angular frequency

ω=B2l2mL

The time period of motion is
⇒  T=2πmLBl

∮E→.dr→=-dϕdt

⇒E×2πr=πμ0nk2R2+r2

⇒E=μ0nkR2r+r2

The radius of the circle traversed by the charged particle is

r=mvqB2

v=Eqtm=μ0nkR2r+r2qtm

⇒μ0nkR2r+r2qtm=qrB2m

⇒μ0nktR2r+r2=rμ0nkt

⇒R2+r22=r2

⇒r=R2

questions.q: There are two solenoids of same length and inductance L but their diameters differ to the extent that one can just fit into the other. They are connected in three different ways in series. (1) They are connected in series but separated by large distance, (2) they are connected in series with one inside the other and senses of the turns coinciding, (3) both are connected in series with one inside the other with senses of the turns opposite as depicted in figures 1, 2 and 3 respectively. The total inductance of the solenoids in each of the case 1, 2 and 3 are respectively
questions.solution:
When two solenoids of inductance L0 are connected in series at large distance and current i is passed through them, the total flux linkage ϕtotalis the sum of the flux linkages L0i and L0i, ie,

                ϕtotal=L0i+L0i

If L be the equivalent inductance of the system, then

               ϕtotal=Li

∴                     Li=L0i+L0i

or L=2L0

When solenoids are connected in series with one inside the other and senses of the turns coinciding, then there will be mutual inductance L between them. In this case the resultant induced emf in the coils is the sum of the emf s e1 and e2 in the respective coils, ie,

                  e=e1+e2

                     =-L0didt±L0didt+-L0didt±L0didt

Where (+) sign is for positive coupling and (-) sign for negative coupling.

But, e=-L.didt

∴         -Ldidt=-L0didt-L0didt±2L0didt

ie,            L=L0+L0+2L0

                    =4L0 (for positive coupling)

When solenoids are connected in series with one inside the other with senses of the turns opposite, then their is negative coupling.

So,                     L=L0+L2-2L0=0

questions.solution:

U=12Li2

Given, U=0.1 J, i=0.2 A

0.1=12L×0.22

⇒ L=2×0.10.22=0.20.2×0.2

=102=5 H

Length of each arm of the rod is L and the angle between the arms is 60° . P is the mid-point of section AC. The magnitude of the magnetic field is B. Then choose the incorrect relation.

OA=OC=L;OP=3L2

questions.q: A long solenoid of the cross-sectional radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> has a thin insulated wire ring tightly put on its winding. One half of the ring has the resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn></math> times that of the other half. The magnetic induction produced by the solenoid varies with time as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></math>, whose b is a constant. If the magnitude of the electric field strength in the ring is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mfrac><mi>R</mi><mi>b</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>q</mi></math> are the smallest positive integers, then what is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>?
questions.solution:
Both upper half and lower half will have same effective area of  π R⁡ 2 2  so charge in flux will be same and induced emf will have some value. But since the resistance is different due to which current must be different but ring is as a whole is closed circuit so electric field will be generated to make the current flow in both parts to be same.





ε + E⁡ π R⁡ - i⁡ 1 0 r⁡ = 0 … i⁡

ε - E⁡ π R⁡ - i⁡r⁡ = 0 … i⁡ i⁡

⇒ 2 E π R⁡ - 9 i⁡ r⁡ = 0

E⁡ = 9 i r 2 π R⁡ ⇒ i⁡ = E⁡ 1 1 r⁡ = π R⁡ 2 b 1 1 r⁡

⇒ E⁡ = 9 r 2 π R⁡ × π R⁡ 2 b 1 1 r⁡ = 9 2 2 Rb

∴ 9 2 2 Rb
